jobs.title: Product Analyst Intern - QuantumBlack, AI by McKinsey at McKinsey & Company
jobs.description: Employer: McKinsey & Company Expires: 10/09/2026 Do you want to do work that matters, alongside supportive leaders who will help you grow faster than you ever thought possible? Are you a creative problem-solver who is energized by challenges? You’ve come to the right place.YOUR IMPACTYou will work as a core member of a multidisciplinary product team, alongside senior product managers, designers, engineers, and technologists, contributing to the development of tech and AI products that create real impact for clients across industries.This full-time summer internship is for bachelor's or master’s students with graduation dates between December 2027 and August 2028 who are pursuing a degree in computer science, business, or a related field, and is expected to last 8-12 weeks.You will support the end-to-end product development lifecycle, from collecting user and market insights to tracking product metrics, refining user stories, and monitoring adoption. You'll collaborate closely with engineering and design counterparts, develop a growing understanding of how great product teams operate, and build the foundational skills needed to contribute to complex, high-stakes product challenges.Your work will help solve some of the most complex and high-impact challenges facing clients across industries. Collaborating across QuantumBlack, AI by McKinsey and QuantumBlack Labs teams, you'll help develop innovative AI and digital product capabilities and scalable enterprise solutions. Your contributions will directly support clients in accelerating AI adoption and solving complex business problems at scale.You'll be based in our Atlanta, Boston, Chicago, or New York office for an 8-12 week internship during the Summer of 2027 as part of our global Product community. Working in cross-functional teams, you'll collaborate closely with data scientists, engineers, designers, and industry experts to deliver AI-enabled products. By partnering with clients from technical teams to C-level executives, you'll help solve complex problems that drive tangible business value and begin to build your skills as a client-facing technologist.Your work offers a unique opportunity to grow at the forefront of AI and product development. You'll develop expertise at the intersection of technology and business by tackling diverse challenges in the evolving AI landscape. Working alongside multidisciplinary teams, you'll gain a holistic understanding of how great products enable advanced AI while collaborating with some of the leading technologists and AI practitioners in the industry.YOUR GROWTHDriving lasting impact and building long-term capabilities with our clients is not easy work. jobs.title: Interpretative Research and Programs Internship at Smithsonian National Museum of African American History and Culture
jobs.description: Employer: Smithsonian National Museum of African American History and Culture Expires: 10/09/2026 NOTE: Applications submitted through Handshake will NOT be considered.Interpretative Research and Programs InternshipHybrid Part-Time Internship and Hybrid Full-Time Internship$425/week and $850/weekJanuary 25 – April 23, 2027Desired Majors and Areas of Study: Museum Studies, Museum Education, African American Studies, Africana/African Diaspora Studies and History, Latin American and Caribbean History, American Studies, Public History, Performance Studies; All encouraged to applyThe Office of Strategic Partnerships (OSP) exists to strengthen the capabilities and sustainability of historical, cultural, and art institutions focused on African American and African Diaspora, which we do through our collaborations with museum service organizations, professional associations, and related organizations.Through collaboration and partnerships, OSP:• Delivers far-reaching and transformative support for under-resourced organizations on a regional, national, and international level;• Connects and builds awareness about the work of its participating institutions;• Provides access to training and resources that support and advance leaders and field-wide best practices.The Interpretative Research and Programs Intern will support the continued development and relaunch of the Ethical Interpretation Workshop, a signature program of the National Museum of African American History and Culture (NMAAHC)/OSP. While ethical interpretation is embedded throughout the Museum’s collections, digital platforms, and exhibitions, no single exhibition exclusively focuses on this topic. This internship will play a key role in advancing both a Smithsonian-wide pilot program and a national workshop dedicated to ethical theory and practice, with particular emphasis on illustrating the historical and contemporary relationships between African American communities and the natural world.The selected intern will contribute to the planning, coordination, and preparation of materials for these initiatives, with primary responsibilities centered on research and administrative support. As time permits, the intern may also assist in organizing and facilitating virtual or in-person professional development programs and meetups for the growing Community of Practice focused on ethical interpretation. The intern will join the planning teams for these efforts and support the development of program-related resources and communications.The project will enable the intern to:Gain hands-on experience in planning, coordinating, and developing program materials for the Smithsonian-wide pilot program and national Ethical Interpretation Workshop;Develop a deep understanding of ethical interpretation theory and practice, particularly as it relates to African American and African Diasporic communities and their relationships with the natural world;Conduct object-specific and biographical research to support workshops, and program development;Build skills in interpreting material culture and historical narratives in ways that are accessible and meaningful to a broad, diverse audience, particularly those interested in African American art, history, and culture;Learn to distill large quantities of multimedia exhibition content into thematic, succinct, and engaging museum tours;Gain insight into exhibition rotation cycles, object display length, and the multidisciplinary nature of museum exhibitions and interpretation;Develop object interpretation, public speaking, storytelling, and audience engagement skills;Meet one-on-one with professionals across the museum and broader cultural sector to explore career paths, professional development, and sector-specific opportunities.Through this internship, the intern will gain exposure to the external-facing work of OSP; the national landscape of interpretive practice; models for presenting sensitive historical content; the relationship between interpretation and tourism; and strategies for partnership development, strategic planning, and problem solving. The experience may include site visits to African American museums, universities, and sites of memory throughout the Washington, D.C. metro area, as well as travel to the Association of African American Museums Annual Conference.The ideal candidate will have some knowledge/appreciation for African American History and Public History, experience with partnership development/outreach, and research, and excellent writing and communication skills.Internship Duties Include (but are not limited to):Participate in an online review and physical walkthrough of all museum exhibition galleries with OSP Staff, and other NMAAHC curators, as availableResearch effective methods of program facilitation and audience engagement techniquesIdentify and research key objects on view in NMAAHC exhibitions that fit within the scope and intended content of this projectDevelop a Smithsonian wide exhibition guide centered around ethical interpretation specifically focusing on the narratives of Africans/African AmericansCreate a presentation and/or talking points for each exhibition guide that can be used by other NMAAHC curators, docents, and museum staff on OSP-centered toursUnderstand how to effectively use multiple interpretative methodologies to create impactful public programs, utilizing audience engagement techniquesObserve Museum leadership and strategic planning initiativesAttend virtual cross-departmental meetings, workshops, and special events

jobs.title: Undergraduate Music and Performing Arts Curatorial Internship at Smithsonian National Museum of African American History and Culture
jobs.description: Employer: Smithsonian National Museum of African American History and Culture Expires: 10/09/2026 NOTE: Applications submitted through Handshake will NOT be considered.Undergraduate Music and Performing Arts Curatorial InternshipPart-Time Hybrid Internship$425/weekJanuary 25 – April 23, 2027Desired Majors and Areas of Study: Museum Studies, Music, Film, Television, Theater History and/or Performance Studies, American historyThis internship is an opportunity to do meaningful curatorial work at one of the most prominent cultural institutions in the country building skills in African American collecting and cultural preservation while expanding professional networks. As part of NMAAHC’s commitment to strengthening the museum talent pipeline, this position is designed to support undergraduate students in gaining foundational knowledge and hands-on experience, while introducing them to the many different career paths that curatorial work can open. The skills developed through this internship (research, writing, object documentation, and professional communication) directly support careers across a wide range of museum positions, including curatorial, collections, education, public programs, and outreach, as well as related fields such as archival work, cultural policy, and the broader nonprofit and public humanities sectors. By the end of the internship the intern will be able to: Navigate and use the TMS (The Museum System) collection information database to locate and support documentation of collection records;Assist with the handling and processing of objects and archival materials following professional conservation and preservation standards;Assist with the creation and review of collection inventories, contributing to the Museum’s collections stewardship goals;Support object research and assist with producing accurate collection documentation as directed by the curator;Research and prepare donor briefs and profiles that support the curator’s donor cultivation and community stewardship efforts;Assist with drafting and editing collection and exhibition texts;Assist with drafting object acquisition proposals using curatorial criteria and an understanding of the museum’s collecting priorities;Produce interpretive labels and an exhibition narrative for a proposed exhibition drawn from the NMAAHC Music & Performing Arts Collection, with support from the curator;Research and write an acquisition proposal with curatorial guidance and present it to the NMAAHC Collections Committee; Develop an understanding of museums as institutions of cultural stewardship and gain insight into the importance of collecting and preservation through direct engagement with the collection and curatorial practice.The Office of Curatorial Affairs advances NMAAHC’s mission of sharing the history and culture of African Americans and all people of African descent with a diverse public by collecting, preserving, researching, and interpreting artifacts of lasting cultural significance. The Music and Performing Arts Curator contributes to this mission by stewarding a collection that spans the full breadth of African American creative expression (including music, television, film, theater, dance, comedy, and popular culture) from everyday creative life to landmark performances, recordings, and cultural movements. All of these areas are available to the intern. As an undergraduate intern, you will assist the curator with collections acquisition and processing, object documentation, research, and writing, supporting an active list of ongoing projects throughout the internship. jobs.description: Employer: Smithsonian National Museum of African American History and Culture Expires: 10/09/2026 NOTE: Applications submitted through Handshake will NOT be considered.Council Oral History Project InternshipHybrid Part-Time Internship$425/weekJanuary 25 – April 19, 2027Desired Majors and Areas of Study: Oral History, Public History, Library Science, Archival Management, Museum Studies, Arts Management, African American History and Cultural Studies, Cultural Heritage and Preservation, Digital Preservation and Records Management, Museum Collections and Collections Management, Nonprofit Leadership and Philanthropy Studies, Archival Research and Information ManagementThe Office of the Director is responsible for guiding the museum’s operation and mission. In coordination with the NMAAHC staff and Council, the Office of the Director oversees the preservation, documentation, display, and dissemination of African American history and culture to a diverse and global audience. The Council Oral History Project Internship provides hands-on experience supporting the preservation and documentation of the history of the National Museum of African American History and Culture (NMAAHC). The internship is a collaborative opportunity between the Office of the Director's Council Relations and Museum Initiatives team and the Oral History Initiative within the Office of Digital Strategies and Engagement. The project focuses on collecting, preserving, and organizing the oral histories of Founding Council members who played a significant role in the creation and development of the museum. This internship is designed to provide hands-on experience in oral history, archival preservation, museum operations, and board relations while developing professional communication, research, and project management skills. Through participation in the Council Oral History Project, the intern will gain practical experience supporting the collection, preservation, and interpretation of historical narratives within a museum setting. The intern will develop a greater understanding of how culturally specific museums operate and how oral history programs support exhibitions, research, collections, and public engagement. Through direct involvement with the Oral History Initiative and Council Relations and Museum Initiatives team, the intern will learn how oral history projects are planned, managed, and implemented from concept through accession into a museum collection.As part of the project, the intern will gain professional experience in archival and oral history practices while supporting the preparation and management of oral history interviews and records. Responsibilities may include archiving Council meeting materials, conducting background research on interview subjects, collecting and organizing oral history documentation, reviewing and proofreading transcripts, writing interview summaries and field notes, preparing collections documentation, observing oral history interviews, and assisting with the planning and implementation of public programs. Key learning objectives include:Developing oral history research and documentation skills through conducting background research, gathering metadata, maintaining records, and supporting interview preparation; Learning archival and digital preservation practices, including transcript review, file management, documentation collection, and preservation workflows; Building professional writing and communication skills by preparing interview summaries, field notes, collections justifications, and other project documentation; Gaining an understanding of board and donor relations through exposure to the museum’s Advisory Council and the Founding Council Oral History Project; Learning ethical standards and best practices in oral history collection as established by the Oral History Association;Developing knowledge of museum collections management and the process of bringing materials into a museum collection;Observing and participating in oral history interviews, including interview preparation, documentation, and post-interview processing;Understanding how oral history content is integrated into museum exhibitions, public programs, and educational initiatives.The internship provides hands-on opportunities through active participation in staff meetings, informational interviews with Smithsonian staff and leadership, oral history documentation, transcript processing, archival research, and public programming support. These experiences allow the intern to apply classroom knowledge in a professional museum environment while developing transferable skills in research, project coordination, records management, writing, digital preservation, and stakeholder engagement. These competencies are highly valuable within the museum field and are also transferable to careers in archives, libraries, public history, cultural heritage organizations, nonprofit management, research institutions, education, communications, and project management. The internship equips participants with both specialized museum knowledge and broadly applicable professional skills that support success across a wide range of industries.This project is important because it preserves the firsthand accounts of the leaders whose vision, advocacy, fundraising efforts, and strategic guidance helped establish NMAAHC. Their experiences provide unique insight into the museum’s creation, from the early efforts to establish the museum through site selection, fundraising, and the museum’s opening. By documenting and preserving these stories, the project ensures that an important part of the museum’s institutional history is available to future researchers, museum professionals, and the public. The internship directly supports the work of both the Council Relations and Museum Initiatives team and the Oral History Initiative. The Council Relations and Museum Initiatives team is responsible for managing the museum’s Advisory Council and advancing museum-wide initiatives, while the Oral History Initiative works to document, preserve, and interpret African American stories through oral history projects that support research, exhibitions, programming, and public engagement. The project aligns closely with NMAAHC’s mission by contributing to the preservation, documentation, and dissemination of African American history and culture. Through oral history collection, archival preservation, and public access initiatives, the project helps ensure that the stories of individuals who shaped the museum and contributed to its success are preserved and shared with diverse audiences for generations to come.The ideal candidate will have a strong interest in oral history, historical research, archives, museum operations, and the preservation and interpretation of African American history and culture. The internship is particularly valuable for students seeking careers in museums, archives, libraries, cultural institutions, public history organizations, and related nonprofit or educational sectors. Preferred qualifications include:Demonstrated interest in oral history interviews and oral history methodology;Interest in African American history, cultural studies, the history of philanthropy, and culturally specific museum leadership; Interest in systems thinking, workflows, and process improvement; Strong organizational skills and attention to detail;Ability to work independently and manage self-directed assignments;Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively both independently and in collaborative team environments.Desired technical and professional competencies include experience or interest in conducting research, reviewing and proofreading written materials, maintaining records and documentation, managing digital files, and supporting archival or oral history projects. Familiarity with Microsoft Office applications, digital collaboration tools, and database or records management systems is beneficial but not required. The selected intern will support the Council Oral History Project through a combination of daily responsibilities, short-term assignments, and long-term projects that provide practical experience in oral history, archival preservation, museum operations, and research. These duties are designed to help the intern achieve the learning objectives of the internship while contributing to the preservation of NMAAHC's institutional history. These responsibilities provide the intern with progressive, hands-on experience in oral history methodology, archival management, research, professional writing, digital preservation, and museum operations while contributing to a project that preserves the stories of the leaders who helped shape the National Museum of African American History and Culture.Internship Duties Include (but are not limited to):Attend staff meetings and mandatory training sessionsParticipate in informational interviews with Smithsonian staff and museum leadershipConduct background research on interview subjects and topics related to oral history projectsCollect, organize, and maintain oral history documentation and project records Review, reformat, proofread, and process oral history transcripts Write interview summaries, field notes, and supporting project documentation Observe oral history interviews and assist with interview preparation and follow-up activitiesSupport the planning and implementation of public programs related to oral history initiativesSupport the archiving and organization of historical Council meeting records for the Council Oral History Project Assist in documenting and preserving oral histories of Council members and other project participants Prepare and compile background research materials that support oral history interviews and project development Assist with metadata collection, records management, and digital preservation activities associated with oral history collections. Draft justifications and supporting documentation for collections-related review processesContribute to ongoing oral history project workflows from interview planning and documentation through transcript processing and archival preparationSupport efforts to make oral history materials accessible for future research, exhibitions, programming, and public engagement

Work designationThis position is fully remote. All core responsibilities are performed independently and do not require a fixed on-site schedule.The team looks for opportunities to meet in person when project timelines and individual schedules align. These gatherings are intentional but informal, driven by shared momentum rather than a fixed cadence. Skipper AI core valuesTrust and Transparency. We communicate openly, follow through on commitments, and treat every client and colleague with honesty. Trust is the foundation of every relationship we build. Humble Hunger. There's more to a failed task than the task itself; every mistake carries a lesson, and progress in anything is still progress forward. It's okay to be wrong, as long as you admit it. What matters is being hungry more often than you are wrong. Have Hard Conversations. One's success in life is directly correlated to their ability to have hard conversations. Conversations are hard if you are passionate, and two passionate people in a room is a rare thing. About Skipper AIIn the last year, we have worked with 8 companies, on countless projects, and have shipped things that did and didn't work. Importantly, we have captured the themes behind what leads to success or failure, and have not found a use case since those learnings did not apply. Skipper AI exists to not skip them. We've driven 90%+ adoption not because of the platform we picked, but because we refuse to skip the intentional steps. Intentionality through change has never been more important. The tools are the easy part; it's the steps most firms rush past, the change management in between where AI actually sticks or quietly dies.

jobs.description: Employer: Pieper Electric, Inc. Expires: 10/10/2026 Project Management InternPosition SummaryThe Project Management Intern supports the safe, efficient, and profitable delivery of electrical construction projects while learning how work moves from estimate and preconstruction through field execution, billing, closeout, and customer follow-up. Working alongside Project Managers, project support team members, field leaders, Estimating, VDC, Prefabrication, Safety, and other partners, the intern assists with project documentation, planning, coordination, material and vendor follow-up, cost awareness, and communication. The internship is designed to provide meaningful project ownership at an appropriate level while building the technical, business, and professional skills needed for an early-career role within Pieper.Values and Ways of WorkingAt Pieper Electric, we believe in the Power to Serve and the Pursuit of Excellence. Interns are expected to demonstrate a Servant's Heart, Wisdom, Integrity, Courage, Humility, and Passion in how they learn, communicate, support the field, and serve customers and teammates. Essential ResponsibilitiesSafety and Field Engagement:Complete required safety orientation and follow all company, customer, and jobsite requirements.Participate in jobsite walks, pre-planning discussions, and hazard-recognition activities with supervision.Promote open communication between field and office teams regarding safety concerns, required information, and work-planning needs.Observe how safety, quality, schedule, productivity, and cost decisions affect one another during project execution. Project Documentation and Coordination:Help obtain, organize, and maintain drawings, specifications, addenda, submittals, RFIs, meeting notes, correspondence, schedules, and other project records.Assist with project startup, estimating handoff, document control, routine reporting, and coordination of defined action items.Support permits, inspections, utility-locate requests, site access needs, and other project-specific requirements as assigned.Track job activity, including materials, equipment, resources, deadlines, and open items; communicate status and potential issues promptly. Preconstruction and Technical Planning:Support basic quantity takeoffs, bid-package preparation, scope review, and comparison of plans, specifications, and addenda.Learn how Estimating, design, layout, VDC/BIM, prefabrication, Trimble/Total Station, scheduling, and operations planning support field installation.Assist with coordination of design, layout, assembly details, prefabrication documentation, and project planning tasks as appropriate to the assignment.Help prepare for project kickoff and participate in the transition of project information from estimating to operations. Planning, Scheduling, and Resource Support:Participate in weekly planning and project meetings; document decisions, owners, deadlines, and follow-up items.Update approved trackers and schedules and help identify constraints that may affect safety, productivity, quality, cost, or completion dates.Support coordination of materials, tools, equipment, information, and internal resources needed by the project team and field.Learn how Project Managers forecast work, monitor progress, and adjust plans based on project conditions. Materials, Vendors, and Project Controls:Request and organize vendor or subcontractor information and quotes as directed; support purchase-order and material-tracking processes within assigned authority.Compile information for material purchases, submittals, delivery coordination, and operation and maintenance manuals.Assist with approved cost coding, expense tracking, billing documentation, change-order logs, and other project-control activities.Develop an understanding of budget, committed cost, labor productivity, forecast, billing, collections, cash flow, and project profitability without independently approving transactions. Communication, Service, and Team Collaboration:Communicate professionally with project managers, field leaders, craftspeople, customers, vendors, and internal partners.Prepare clear meeting notes, status updates, reports, presentations, and project correspondence for review.Provide timely, accurate service and escalate questions, conflicts, customer concerns, and project risks to the appropriate leader.Seek feedback, demonstrate curiosity, protect confidential information, and contribute ideas that improve team coordination and project outcomes. Closeout and Continuous Improvement:Assist with punch-list tracking, as-built documentation, operation and maintenance manuals, warranty information, final billing support, and closeout packages.Help confirm that required project records are complete, accurate, organized, and transferred or archived appropriately.Participate in lessons-learned discussions and complete an internship capstone that recommends or demonstrates a practical project improvement. QualificationsCurrently pursuing an associate or bachelor’s degree in construction management, Construction Science, Electrical or Mechanical Engineering, Building Science, Business, or a related field; equivalent technical education or relevant experience may be considered.Interest in electrical construction, project management, estimating, engineering, or field operations.Basic proficiency with Microsoft Office, including Excel, Word, Outlook, and Teams; willingness to learn company project systems and technical tools.Ability to travel locally to project sites and work in both office and active construction environments, as the assignment requires.Core Skills and BehaviorsPositive safety attitude and personal integrity - both are non-negotiable.Curiosity, initiative, accountability, and willingness to ask questions and apply feedback.Clear verbal and written communication with strong attention to detail.Ability to organize multiple priorities, maintain accurate records, and meet deadlines.Respectful, service-oriented approach when working with field and office employees, customers, and vendors.Work Environment and Physical RequirementsThe internship includes office and jobsite work. Office responsibilities may require extended periods of sitting, standing, and computer use. Jobsite visits may involve walking or standing for extended periods, stairs or uneven surfaces, outdoor conditions, noise, and required personal protective equipment. Reasonable accommodation may be made for qualified individuals.

jobs.description: Employer: Clark Construction Group Expires: 10/10/2026 At Clark, we build leaders—individuals who take ownership, rise to challenges, and deliver the Clark standard of excellence. Across the industry, Clark is known for exceptional performance and shaping communities through some of the most complex, high-profile projects being built today.We empower you to take on significant responsibility early, backing your growth with extensive resources, mentorship, formal training, and a culture that challenges you to advance your career further. Here, the standard is higher. Our team doesn't just build landmark projects—we build the leaders who make them possible. The RoleThe Summer Associate Program is your opportunity to build a comprehensive understanding of the construction industry and our business. As a summer associate, you will be fully embedded with a team on a jobsite or in a department, gaining hands-on experience across project management, field management, project development, and business operations. Beyond your project work, you will become an integrated member of the Clark community through training and development opportunities. Build your network through social events and jobsite tours, and sharpen your skills with formal training sessions led by Clark experts. Other cornerstones of the Summer Associate Program include: The Capstone Project: A team-based project that challenges you to develop innovative solutions for real-time business opportunities. You will present your findings directly to company leadership, gaining visibility and the chance to make a tangible impact.The Passport Experience: A curated series of experiences designed to guide your summer journey. The Passport showcases the full breadth of Clark’s business, helps you establish meaningful connections across the company, and ensures you gain essential industry knowledge. This immersive, full-time program runs for 8 -10 weeks and begins in late May or early June. Responsibilities Throughout the summer, you will be exposed to:Project Management: Working in project management gives you an understanding of the day-to-day and long-term business and financial management associated with construction projects.Financial Management - Review gross billings, track change orders, and subcontractor requisitions Document Control - Manage the submittals, RFI, and material tracking process Trade Partner Success - Become a trusted advisor to our subcontractors to plan for a successful field installationField Management: Learn the intricacies of the building process, assist in site logistics, and ensure quality and safety on our jobsites.Quality Control and Safety - Monitor tradeworkers with emphasis on the quality of work and safetyProject Schedule - Assist with schedule management and site logistics Critical Thinking - Resolve unforeseen challenges within installation, schedule, and trade partner coordinationProject Development: Understand how we acquire new work, develop winning strategies, and build strong client relationships through budgeting, estimating, and purchasingBudgeting - Review initial contract documents, solicit, and provide preliminary evaluations of subcontractor bidsEstimating - Perform quantity takeoffs, prepare the overall bid proposal, and quantify labor and material prices required for projects Purchasing - Collaborate to execute subcontractor agreements, review the scope of work, and manage relationships with subcontractorsBusiness Operations: Explore the essential functions that keep our company running smoothly, gaining a holistic view of the Clark organization. Basic QualificationsPursuing an undergraduate degree or equivalent, or a graduate degreeInterest and passion for the construction industry What a Successful Candidate Looks LikeWe look for individuals who embody these core principles:Enthusiasm & Drive: Be punctual and dedicated, staying until work is done. Arrive early for meetings and events. Be a proactive team player – ask how you can help and be present. Take initiative, represent the company professionally (dress, demeanor), and build trust with your team, clients, and stakeholders. Proactively seek ways to contribute to team success, and always maintain a positive attitude.Delivery & Performance: Reliably meet the expectations of your role and commitments. Understand and follow Clark's standard procedures. Take on new responsibilities, dig into the details, and bring solutions to problems. Take ownership, be accountable, and demonstrate responsiveness with a sense of urgency.Learning & Growth: Immerse yourself in Clark's culture, your team, and your community. Fulfill Clark Corporate University learning requirements. Be engaged, accountable, and self-directed in your learning – be curious! Continuously build your technical expertise and grow your business acumen. The work environment and requirements described below are representative of those necessary for an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this role. The Physical Side of the Role: This is an active, hands-on role. You can expect to be on your feet frequently, navigating active job sites with uneven terrain, stairs, ladders, and hoists. The work is physically demanding and requires a full range of motion, including bending, kneeling, and reaching. You’ll need to be comfortable frequently lifting and carrying materials up to 25 pounds, and occasionally up to 50 pounds. This role requires the ability to communicate effectively, as well as visual acuity for reading plans and inspecting work. The role does include desk time in the office that may require prolonged periods of sitting for tasks like computer work, document review, and meetings.Your Work Environment: You’ll spend a significant amount of your time on active construction sites, which means being adaptable to all kinds of weather and moderate to loud noise levels, and comfortable in elevated or confined work areas with moving mechanical equipment and with the fast-paced nature of a project in progress. You will also spend time in a typical office setting with moderate noise levels. Your safety is our top priority, and you'll be expected to follow Clark Construction's safety policies and procedures, and all applicable laws, at all locations.Our High-Performing Culture: This is a demanding, high-performance environment. We are looking for candidates who are energized by challenge, thrive under pressure, and are prepared to do what it takes to achieve exceptional results. Success in this role requires significant commitment, including flexibility to work extended hours, especially during critical project phases or client deadlines.A Drug Free Workplace: Clark promotes a drug free workplace. A pre-employment fitness for duty screening is required, and random fitness for duty tests of employees are conducted quarterly.

jobs.feedName: Mike Curb College of Arts, Media, & Communication
jobs.title: Graphic Design Intern at Marketing for Change
jobs.description: Employer: Marketing for Change Expires: 10/11/2026 The Change Academy at Marketing for Change offers graduate students, college seniors, recent graduates and other emerging creatives a paid semester-long experience working and learning at one of the nation’s leading behavior-change marketing agencies. In behavior-change marketing, the objective is not sales or profits; it’s influencing behaviors in a way that leads to a healthier, safer, more sustainable world. We’re looking for a Graphic Design & Creative Intern who wants to put their creative skills to work on real projects with real impact. You’ll work alongside our creative team and other experts across the agency, gaining hands-on experience developing visual concepts and creative work for campaigns designed to make a difference. As part of the Change Academy, you’ll have opportunities to contribute to real client work while strengthening your design skills and learning how behavioral science informs creative strategy. Depending on the project, your work may include graphic design, visual concepting, campaign creative, digital and social content, presentation design, and other visual storytelling. You’ll receive mentorship and skill-specific training from experienced creatives, along with broader training in behavioral science and behavior-change marketing. You’ll also participate in agency events, client meetings and, if you want, off-the-clock social gatherings. Interns earn $18.40 an hour or minimum wage (whichever is higher) and work 20 hours a week, with at least one day a week in our offices. The in-office experience is critical to helping interns improve their skills, work directly with mentors and share a group experience with their cohort. Please confirm you can participate in person at your selected location. LocationOur work hubs are located in Orlando and just outside Washington, DC, and we very much prefer to hire people willing to locate in those areas. We are mostly a hybrid workforce with staff working together in-person at least one day a week because we value the fun and collaboration that allows. The program lasts between 12 and 16 weeks depending on the semester. Instruction takes place during the first 6 to 8 weeks of the internship, mixed with group projects and real work experience. The final weeks focus on work experience and give interns an opportunity to build their portfolios with meaningful, professional creative experience. The Change Academy is the main path to entry-level employment at Marketing for Change. Several former M4C interns are now in leadership roles at M4C, including an art director, creative director, senior media planner and strategist. What we’re looking for:Relevant experience, coursework or training in graphic design, visual communication, advertising, art direction or a related creative field. Preference is given to graduate students, recent graduates or college seniors with at least one prior internship or comparable creative experience. Other adults with the right skills but no degree may also apply. Several have been successful in the past.A portfolio or work samples that show your design skills, creative thinking and visual point of view. School, internship, freelance and personal projects are all welcome.Familiarity with common design tools and an interest in continuing to build your creative and technical skills.A willingness to take feedback, try new ideas and collaborate with other creatives, strategists and agency teams.Deep curiosity about what makes people tick and how design can influence what people notice, feel and do.An interest in using your creative powers for good and making the world a better place.Being a nice person. Seriously. We want the kind of person most other people love to work with. A quick note about our hiring processApplying for a job can feel a little like sending your application out into the void and hoping a real person is on the other side. At Marketing for Change, one will be. Real people on our team review every application. We may use technology to make parts of the process easier, but when it comes to getting to know you, considering what you could bring to our team and making hiring decisions, that’s us. We know there’s a real person on the other side of every application, too. Someone who gave us their time, shared a little bit of their story and decided we might be worth exploring. We don’t take that lightly. And if you’re considering us, we’re genuinely glad you’re here. Note: Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States. Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a background check and Form I-9 Employment Eligibility Verification. TimingSeptember 2026 to January 2027

jobs.title: Golf Internship @ Bandon Dunes Golf Resort at Bandon Dunes Golf Resort
jobs.description: Employer: Bandon Dunes Golf Resort Expires: 10/14/2026 As a Golf Intern at Bandon Dunes Golf Resort, you'll get real hands-on experience at one of the world's top golf destinations while pursuing your Professional Golf Management degree. You'll work directly with guests, manage our golf shop, coordinate tournaments, and learn the business side of golf operations. This isn't just shadowing someone—you'll have actual responsibilities that matter to our guests' experiences on courses that rank among the top 16 public courses in America.About Bandon Dunes Golf Resort:Bandon Dunes is a world-class golf resort located on the Oregon Coast near the charming community of Bandon. Guests come to experience golf as it was meant to be at Bandon Dunes' six distinct golf courses. That includes five 18-hole courses, which all rank among the top 16 public courses in the United States, according to Golf Digest. The resort is also home to an award-winning par-3 course, Bandon Preserve. A second par-3 course, Shorty's, will open in 2024. The two short courses are 'Courses with a Mission,' with all net proceeds funding the Bandon Dunes Charitable Foundation. The Foundation supports communities along the South Coast of Oregon.Beyond premier golf, guests delight in a variety of dining options at Bandon Dunes’ collection of restaurants. Whether you're looking to enjoy locally-sourced, Pacific-Northwest cuisine accompanied by an award-winning wine list, or prefer kicking back in a Scottish-style setting with traditional pub fare and local microbrews, there is something for everyone.Working at Bandon Dunes is a dream for golf fans, outdoor enthusiasts, and hospitality professionals alike. The Bandon Dunes team works together to create trips of a lifetime for our guests. We are passionate stewards of our resort, our community, and our environment. As an endlessly curious group, we ask questions, share ideas, and always look for a better way. With a hard-working attitude, we help guide our guests through their pure golf experience, immersed in Oregon’s natural beauty and away from the demands of daily life.What You'll Do:Learn the retail side of golf. You'll become an expert on our golf shop merchandise, help guests find what they need, and handle special orders. This means understanding products well enough to make real recommendations, not just ringing up sales.Handle real transactions. You'll process merchandise sales, greens fees, and equipment rentals while keeping accurate records. You'll learn the financial side of golf operations through actual daily work, not textbook theory.Provide genuine customer service. You'll answer guest questions, schedule tee times, and maintain professional phone interactions. When guests call, you'll be the voice they hear representing Bandon Dunes.Support tournaments and events. You'll help organize competitions and special events, coordinating between different departments to make sure everything runs smoothly. This is where you'll see how all the moving pieces fit together.Manage inventory and operations. You'll help keep merchandise displays organized, assist with inventory counts, and support various services like handicapping systems and driving range operations.What Makes You a Great Fit:You're pursuing a Professional Golf Management degree. We work with certified PGM programs and prefer students who can commit to a 6-month internship. This gives you enough time to really learn the business, not just get a quick overview.You communicate well. Strong written and verbal skills matter here because you'll interact with guests from around the world. You need to sound professional on the phone and explain complex golf services clearly.You can handle multiple priorities. Golf operations move fast, and you'll need to manage several tasks while staying calm under pressure. If you get flustered easily when things get busy, this probably isn't the right fit.You're flexible with your schedule. Golf doesn't stop for weekends or holidays. You'll work evenings, weekends, and busy periods when our guests need us most.Special Intern Benefits:Shared staff housing available for a reasonable fee, mentorship from industry professionals, and the chance to play golf for free on seven award-winning courses.If you're serious about a career in golf and want to learn the business at one of the world's premier destinations, we'd like to hear from you. This internship will give you real experience you can't get in a classroom, plus the chance to build relationships with industry professionals. You'll work hard, but you'll also get to play some of the best golf of your life on your days off.Ready to embark on an enriching journey in the world of golf? Apply today to become a Golf Intern at Bandon Dunes Golf Resort and be part of a team dedicated to providing one of the world’s most exceptional golfing experiences.At Bandon Dunes Golf Resort, we are proud to be an equal-opportunity employer. We value diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

jobs.title: Getty Post-Baccalaureate Conservation Internship at J. Paul Getty Trust
jobs.description: Employer: J. Paul Getty Trust Expires: 10/15/2026 The Getty Post-Baccalaureate Conservation Internships aim to increase the number of students from underrepresented backgrounds preparing to enroll in graduate degree programs related to museum conservation. An advanced degree is essential to a conservation career and few programs exist. Applicants often boost their credentials by completing prerequisite courses and undertaking up to thousands of hours of conservation training, usually unpaid. Graduate program administrators say these realities have limited opportunities for underrepresented groups.Launched in 2020 as a pilot program, the Getty Post-Baccalaureate Internships are the first nationwide effort to provide yearlong financial support and hands-on conservation experience to underrepresented post-baccalaureates who are preparing to apply to conservation graduate programs. EligibilityWhile these internships are intended for students from backgrounds underrepresented in the conservation field, Getty encourages eligible candidates from all backgrounds to apply for consideration. Getty is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any protected trait under the law. Candidates will have the opportunity to demonstrate their interest in museum conservation and how they might add new and underrepresented perspectives, which can include – among other things – socio-economic status, cultural background, physical or other disability, geographical origin, and/or any other life experiences.Candidates must:-Be a United States citizen or permanent resident eligible to work in the United States (permanent residents are non-citizens authorized to live and work in the United States on a permanent basis, also known as "green card" holders). Those with DACA (Deferred Action for Childhood Arrival) status valid through the internship period are also eligible.-Be committed to a career in conservation and possess a strong desire to attend graduate school to further that goal.-Be able to demonstrate previous experience in conservation. Terms of the GrantAll positions are full-time for 12 months from September 7, 2027 — August 25, 2028. Interns are placed at conservation studios and labs at the Getty Center or Getty Villa for their first six months, and then at a local Los Angeles museum or within a different Getty department for the second six months.Grant AmountThe grant amount is $45,500 for 12 months plus $1,500 towards relocation expenses to Los Angeles. The internship includes an additional $4,000 towards educational reimbursements, certificate courses in conservation, domestic conservation conference attendance, or other professional-development opportunities related to the internship. Housing is not provided. Interns are eligible to enroll in Getty's healthcare plan at a subsidized cost. Please note that grant funds may be subject to federal and state taxes and deductions.Prerequisite Course for Graduate SchoolDuring spring 2028, interns may enroll in a prerequisite course (chemistry, art history, studio art, and/or foreign language) at a local community college to help fulfill the requirements for their graduate school applications. In addition to support from their supervisors, interns will also have the support of an academic advisor Collaborating InstitutionsInternships are offered at the conservation studios and labs at the Getty Center in Los Angeles and the Getty Villa in Malibu, along with local Los Angeles museums. For the 2027-2028 internship year, placements are being offered at the following Getty departments and institutions:Getty Conservation Institute Collections Department and Los Angeles County Museum of ArtGetty Conservation Institute Science Department and The HuntingtonGetty Research Institute Conservation and Preservation Department and the Autry Museum of the American WestJ. Paul Getty Museum Antiquities Conservation Department and the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences Margaret Herrick Library

jobs.description: Employer: Centrus Energy Expires: 10/16/2026 Job Summary:Ready to see how planning, data, and organization help keep major projects moving? As a Project Controls Intern at Centrus Energy, you’ll gain hands-on experience supporting projects at our American Centrifuge Plant (ACP) in Piketon, Ohio. Working alongside experienced project controls and project management professionals, you’ll learn how teams use schedules, budgets, performance data, and project information to monitor progress and support successful project delivery. This internship offers practical experience that can launch a future career in project controls, project management, engineering, or business operations.What You Will Do:Step into the world of project controls and help teams understand where projects stand and where they’re headed. jobs.description: Employer: United States Golf Association Expires: 10/17/2026 The USGA is a mission-based golf organization whose purpose is to unify the golf community through handicapping and grassroots programs; to showcase the game’s best talent through the U.S. Open, U.S. Women’s Open and 13 other national championships and our museum; to provide unbiased global governance with The R&A through the playing, equipment and Amateur Status rules; and to advance issues important to golf’s future, with a focus on driving sustainability, accessibility and inclusion. As a nonprofit association, our work and our team are driven to act for the good of the game. The USGA’s headquarters are located in Liberty Corner, NJ, with a recently opened campus in Pinehurst, NC. For more, visit usga.org. About this role: The USGA Golf Museum and Library seeks a recent graduate or currently enrolled student in Library Science or Archival Studies for a paid internship in the nation’s oldest sports museum. Founded in 1936, the USGA Golf Museum is the world’s leading institution for the collection, preservation, interpretation and dissemination of golf history. Since 1936, the Museum has connected golfers, sports fans and scholars with remarkable artifacts, documents, images and stories that chronicle golf’s rich history. The USGA Special Collections contain over 500,000 catalogued items including championship and personal archives, institutional records, rare books, club histories, yardage guides, comic books, fiction, poetry, historic and contemporary periodicals, instruction, biographies, newspapers, sheet music, comic books, cookbooks, programs, tour guides, directories, reference material, green section material, golf course care and maintenance, historic dealer and manufacturer catalogs for clothing, gear, and equipment, and more documenting the history of the game and all of its aspects in more than 10 languages and from around the world. Original material dates from 1566 with the Scottish Acts of Parliament to the present day. Items are used for both exhibits and research to inform content and create scholarship on the history and future of the game. The USGA Golf Museum Special Collections Intern will assist with numerous projects supporting the Special Collections. S/he will gain valuable experience in several areas of library operations including hands-on work with historic materials, describing and cataloging material in a digital repository, digitization of archival material, research, and other tasks within the USGA Special Collections. This internship is a unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience archiving, preserving and making available to the public materials on the history of golf. What you’ll do:Collections Processing and CatalogingSupport all aspects of archival collections processing including arrangement, description and cataloging materials in the Museum’s collections management system, TMS CollectionsDevelop familiarity with the TMS Record Style Guide to standardize existing TMS records for Library and Special Collections recordsSupport the Library and Special Collections digitization program by digitizing archival material and ensuring proper metadata cataloging in TMS Collections and TMS Media StudioAdditional collections processing projects as directedCollections ManagementEnsure proper housing of archival materialsSupport movement and reshelving of materials across all collections storage locationsAdditional collections management projects as directedResearch and EngagementAssist with research requests and onsite research visitsSupport the preparation and organization of assets for Museum exhibitions and projects to promote the collections Additional research projects as directed Where you’ll be: This role will be based at our Liberty Corner, NJ campus, working approximately 20 hours per week, ideally with 3 days per week on-site, between Monday - Friday. An academic semester is requested though opportunity exists for a 12-month internship. What you bring:Currently enrolled or recent graduate of a graduate level program in Library ScienceBasic knowledge of digital asset management systemsBasic knowledge of metadata, library standards and resources, and a desire to assist in preservation and access of library materialAbility to lift and move library materials up to 25 poundsBasic knowledge of best practices in handling sensitive and historic materialsPassion and enthusiasm for history and the care of historic materialsAppreciation and interest in sports heritage and/or the game of golf Compensation: The rate of pay is $20 per hour, plus overtime in accordance with applicable New Jersey law. The USGA is an equal opportunity employer. Our organization believes we are stronger by embracing our diverse backgrounds and perspectives, promoting equity so all teammates can excel and grow in their careers, and fostering experiences to drive inclusion in our workplace and game. Golf is a game for everyone, and you are always welcome.

jobs.description: Employer: United States Golf Association Expires: 10/17/2026 The USGA is a mission-based golf organization whose purpose is to unify the golf community through handicapping and grassroots programs; to showcase the game’s best talent through the U.S. Open, U.S. Women’s Open and 13 other national championships and our museum; to provide unbiased global governance with The R&A through the playing, equipment and Amateur Status rules; and to advance issues important to golf’s future, with a focus on driving sustainability, accessibility and inclusion. As a nonprofit association, our work and our team are driven to act for the good of the game. The USGA’s headquarters are located in Liberty Corner, NJ, with a recently opened campus in Pinehurst, NC. For more, visit usga.org. About this role The USGA Golf Museum and World Golf Hall of Fame seeks a recent graduate or currently enrolled student in Museum Studies for a paid internship in the nation’s oldest sports museum. Founded in 1936, the USGA Golf Museum is the world’s leading institution for the collection, preservation, interpretation and dissemination of golf history. Since 1936, the Museum has connected golfers, sports fans and scholars with remarkable artifacts, documents, images and stories that chronicle golf’s rich history. The Museum Collection comprises more than 85,000 catalogued objects documenting the history of golf from its origins to the present. Included in the collection are artifacts from some of the most important moments in the history of championship golf. Highlights of the collection include Alan Shepard’s Moon Club; works of art by Rembrandt, Norman Rockwell, Andy Warhol, Salvador Dali and Roy Lichtenstein; a trophy from the 1904 Olympic games; rare and significant artifacts from World Wars I and II and an extensive collection of memorabilia from U.S. Presidents. The Museum Collections Intern will assist with numerous projects supporting the Museum Collection. S/he will gain valuable experience in several areas of collections care including hands-on work related to object handling, cataloging and rehousing of collections. The Museum Collections Intern will assist the collections team in the large-scale rehousing and reorganization project and can expect to make significant contributions to improving data standardization and storage conditions. This internship is a unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience working with a unique museum collection. What you’ll do:Collections CareAssist with long-term, large-scale collections projects including rehousing and cataloging of artifactsSupport rehousing and movement of materials across all collections storage locationsSupport collections team in receiving and releasing shipments, packing artifacts for transport and condition reportingSupport collections team in gallery maintenance through climate monitoring and integrated pest managementAdditional collections management projects as directed Collections Processing and CatalogingCataloging materials in the Museum’s collection’s management system, TMS CollectionsDevelop familiarity with the TMS Record Style Guide to standardize existing TMS records for Museum records Additional cataloging projects as directed Where you’ll beThis role will be based at our Liberty Corner, NJ campus, working approximately 20 hours per week, ideally with 3 days per week on-site, between Monday - Friday. The intern should be able to commit to at least one full semester. What you bringCurrently enrolled student or recent graduate of an MA program in Museum Studies or related fieldAbility to work independently with strong organizational skills and attention to detailAbility to think creatively and thoughtfully when faced with unique storage needs and willingness to voice opinions on housing methodsWillingness to work collaboratively with team membersProficiency in Microsoft Office productsExperience with museum databases a plusCompensation: The rate of pay is $20 per hour, plus overtime in accordance with applicable New Jersey law. The USGA is an equal opportunity employer. Our organization believes we are stronger by embracing our diverse backgrounds and perspectives, promoting equity so all teammates can excel and grow in their careers, and fostering experiences to drive inclusion in our workplace and game. Golf is a game for everyone, and you are always welcome.

Ahold Delhaize USA associates support the brands with a wide range of services, including Finance, Legal, Sustainability, Commercial, Digital and E-commerce, Technology and more.Internship Overview:Get an insider view of the fast-changing grocery retail industry while developing relevant business, technical and leadership skills geared towards enhancing your career. This role will report to the Manager of Product Strategy for the edge platform, with the potential for exposure to other product areas dependent on performance and workload.Requirements:Currently pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Economics, Mathematics, Business Administration, Business Management, or related fields.Experience with or understanding of major digital media channels and their key KPIs, as well as how they fit into the marketing funnel.Developing technical fluency - ability to speak to technical aspects of digital products and effectively communicate them to various audiences, from engineers to salespeople.Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to write clear and concise briefs/status updates.Comfortable working in a lean and agile environment, with potentially changing priorities, inconsistent day-to-day workloads, and exposure to leadership.Experience with data tools like Power Bi, BigQuery, Tableau, Python, SQL, or similar tool.Individual cohort pay rates vary based on location, academic year, and position.Non-Tech Roles:ME/NC/PA/SC Salary Range: $18.10 - $34.20IL/MA/MD Salary Range: $20.00 - $37.80

jobs.title: VESTER Campus Ambassador at Golden Hire Consulting
jobs.description: Employer: Golden Hire Consulting Expires: 10/18/2026 Join the Founding Team at VESTERYou buy a coffee at Starbucks. Instead of earning points, you earn Starbucks stock.That’s VESTER.VESTER powers stockback rewards — infrastructure that enables brands to reward customers with their own stock instead of traditional loyalty points.We’re growing quickly and hand-selecting some of the sharpest, most connected students on campus to help introduce VESTER to the next generation of investors and consumers.Why Join VESTER? Work Directly With the FoundersReceive direct mentorship from VESTER’s founding team, with experience spanning Société Générale, J.P. Morgan, and Goldman Sachs. There’s no middle layer — you’ll work closely with the people building the company. Get Paid for GrowthEarn compensation for every classmate you successfully sign up, with additional bonuses for reaching growth milestones.Learn Fintech, Markets & SalesGain hands-on exposure to how financial markets, fintech startups, customer acquisition, and enterprise sales operate before your first major internship. Build Your RésuméAdd meaningful startup experience to your résumé while becoming one of the first students involved with VESTER.Top-performing ambassadors will also receive early access to future opportunities as the company scales.Exclusive VESTER MerchRepresent VESTER on campus with exclusive company merchandise and ambassador gear, available to members of the campus ambassador team.Who We’re Looking ForYou might be a strong fit if:You’re connected. You’re active in clubs, Greek life, sports teams, student organizations, residence halls, or campus group chats.You’re curious. You’re interested in markets, investing, fintech, startups, or entrepreneurship. Prior experience is not required.You’re growth-minded. You take initiative, experiment with new ideas, and enjoy figuring out how to get people excited about something new.You’re an operator. You don’t wait around for instructions — you find opportunities and execute.You’re a student. Freshmen and sophomores are especially encouraged to apply, although juniors and seniors are welcome.What You’ll DoAs a VESTER Campus Ambassador, you’ll help grow VESTER within your university community by:Introducing students to VESTER and the concept of stockback rewardsDriving student sign-ups through your campus networkBuilding awareness through clubs, organizations, teams, and student communitiesTesting creative campus growth strategiesSharing feedback directly with VESTER’s founding teamHelping shape VESTER’s early campus growth strategyWhy Now?VESTER is only selecting a handful of ambassadors per campus.Joining now means getting involved at an early stage, working directly with the founding team, and helping shape how VESTER grows across universities.The strongest candidates will be considered first.

jobs.feedName: Mike Curb College of Arts, Media, & Communication
jobs.title: Sales Summer Internship at Packaging Corporation of America
jobs.description: Employer: Packaging Corporation of America Expires: 10/18/2026 As a Fortune 500 company, Packaging Corporation of America (PCA) is an ideas and solutions company. Our corrugated packaging business seeks to be the leader in helping our customers — large and small — package, transport and display products of all kinds. Our white paper business delivers Paper With Purpose by providing the highest level of customer service and operational excellence. We have approximately 15,000 team members in more than 100 locations in the United States that strive to meet the local needs of our customers. Our mission is to serve the needs of our customers, today and tomorrow, with products and services that exceed expectations for performance and environmental responsibility. People • Customers • Trust Program Overview: PCA’s 13-week (May – August) Sales Summer Internship offers hands-on experience across key departments of Design, Production, Customer Service, and Sales while building foundational sales knowledge. Interns will also participate in a corporate office visit in Lake Forest, IL to engage with marketing, meet with PCA leadership, and network with fellow summer interns. Upon successful completion of the program, interns may be offered a full-time position to begin after graduation into PCA’s GIFT Program (rotational sales development program). Principle Accountabilities include:Each intern will be paired with a mentor to guide their development throughout the summerWork on special projects assigned to assist each business function of Design, Customer Service, Production and Sales.Understand PCA’s business, industry, and sales processBuild core sales skills: communication, presentation, time management, problem-solving, and networkingAssist with customer communication: inquiries, new items, lead follow-up, and complaint resolutionBuild a prospect list and visit customers with experienced Sales RepresentativesPresent a final project to the management team and fellow interns Educational Requirements:Must be currently enrolled student majoring in Sales, Marketing, Business or related discipline and have completed their freshman year. A minimum grade point average of 3.0/4.0 is required Must be eligible to work in the US on a full-time basisAbilities/Skills:Strong written, verbal and interpersonal skills are essentialMust be comfortable engaging with mentors, team members and customersCandidate must display maturity and a high level of professionalismMust be able to handle multiple projects or customer inquiries simultaneouslyMust be able to travel. PCA is an Equal Opportunity Employer – Veterans/Disabled and other protected categories All Qualified applicants must submit their resume to careers.packagingcorp.com COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS Starting salary for position: $25.00 - $30.00 per hour determined by your academic year.Paid Holidays.Upon hire, an employee is automatically enrolled in the 401k plan. The plan offers both pre-tax and Roth contribution options along with employer provided matching contributions.Disclaimer: The Compensation and Benefits information in this posting represents PCA’s good faith and reasonable estimate of what it may pay for this position. The Company reserves the right to modify this information at any time, subject to applicable law. PCA is an Equal Opportunity EmployerQualified Applicants must apply at careers.packagingcorp.com to be considered.

jobs.title: Construction Management Intern - Regional at ArchKey Solutions
jobs.description: Employer: ArchKey Solutions Expires: 10/18/2026 Construction Management Intern - Regional About ArchKeyArchKey is one of the nation’s largest privately held specialty trade installation and integrated facility service companies. We design, build, and maintain electrical technologies and specialty systems that power the places where people live, work, and connect.We’re the POWER behind making the improbable possible, electrifying the nation, energizing the future, and bringing communities to life. Our work shapes what’s next, and our people are at the heart of it. At ArchKey, you’ll have the opportunity to learn, grow, and build a career with a team helping power the future.About the PositionOur summer internship program provides hands-on exposure to the electrical construction industry while preparing you for your career after graduation. Working closely with a project manager, you’ll gain experience across project coordination, safety, estimating, scheduling, customer communication, and financial performance. This opportunity is designed for students who are excited to build a career in electrical construction.Regional OpportunityThis position is based within one of ArchKey’s regional markets (New Castle, PA, Clinton, MD, Minneapolis, MN, Fargo, ND, San Jose, CA, Fenton, MO) and supports projects in the surrounding area. Your internship assignment will be connected to a regional office and may include work across multiple active projects, depending on business needs.ArchKey has regional offices and project locations throughout the United States. Visit ArchKey.com to explore our locations and learn more about opportunities in your area. Specific office, project, and assignment details will be shared during the interview process.Day in the LifeAs an intern, you’ll support the project team and gain exposure to the day-to-day work involved in delivering a successful electrical construction project. You may:Support project planning, scheduling, documentation, and coordination.Assist with estimating, bid proposals, purchasing, payments, and change orders.Work with project managers, superintendents, foremen, subcontractors, general contractors, and customers.Gain hands-on exposure to project safety practices and OSHA requirements.Help monitor project progress, budget, quality, and schedule.Assist with engineering and other project-related activities as needed.Minimum QualificationsCurrently enrolled in a degree program in Engineering, Construction Management, Project Management, Business, or a related field.Strong interest in pursuing a career in the electrical construction industry.Strong written and verbal communication skills.Ability to work collaboratively and build effective relationships.Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality.Prior construction experience is a plus.Experience with Bluebeam Revu, Accubid, or other construction technology is a plus.Ability to successfully complete a background check and drug screen.Benefits At ArchKey Solutions, our benefits package includes competitive health insurance options (medical, dental, and vision), a robust 401(k) retirement savings plan with employer match, paid time off and holidays, and access to wellness programs. Additionally, we offer professional development opportunities, tuition reimbursement, and employee assistance programs to support your growth and well-being. We ensure that our benefits are designed to promote the health, security, and work-life balance of our employees. Additional information is available at Archkey.com. Legal & Fraud Disclaimer All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran. We are an Affirmative Action, Equal Opportunity Employer.Beware of fraudulent job postings. ArchKey Solutions only communicates through official channels. All official communication will come from an @archkey.com email address and we will never ask for financial information, payments, or personal details outside of the standard hiring process. To confirm the legitimacy of a job, visit our careers page or reach out to a member of our Talent Acquisition team.

creative, digitally fluent AI Content Marketing Intern to help us turn our existing original content into compelling and innovative digital content across websites, social media, newsletters, and audio and video platforms.This is an ideal opportunity for a current undergraduate, graduate student, or recent graduate who is interested in marketing, gen AI, social media, content creation, business, leadership, and the future of work.You do not need years of professional marketing experience.What matters most is that you are curious, a strong communicator, comfortable experimenting with AI, have good judgment and taste, and are motivated to learn quickly.You’ll work with a substantial library of original content from international keynote speaker, author, and leadership expert Nick Jankel and his company Switch On Leadership.The core challenge is simple:How can we take one great original idea and intelligently and creatively turn it into many different pieces of high-quality content that drive a decent ROI?What You’ll DoUse AI to Repurpose Original ContentTake original articles, book chapters, keynote slides, live videos etc and use AI tools to help transform them into content for different audiences and platforms.For example, using our AI projects with smart instructions, you might turn one book chapter into:A long-form blog post with FAQs and AI search-optimized contentA LinkedIn post and/or articleA more thoughtful Substack articleAn Instagram post or carouselAn AI-generated video for YTA shorter video for YT Shorts, TikTok, IGWebsite landing pageShort social media share quotes and visual contentEmail newsletter materialYou’ll learn how to use AI and strategic, multi-format thinking to adapt an idea for each platform rather than simply copy and paste the same content everywhere.Create AI-Assisted Video / Audio ContentHelp us experiment with the rapidly developing world of AI video.You may:Turn written articles into video scriptsCreate short-form videos from written contentRepurpose longer videos into clipsAdd subtitles, visuals and B-rollCreate YouTube Shorts, TikToks, Reels and LinkedIn videosExperiment with AI video, voice, animation and image-generation toolsTurn articles into podcastsHelp create thumbnails and supporting graphicsUsing AI platforms to pitch to podcastsYou do not need to arrive knowing every tool.
