This could include:Formatting articles in Wix and WordPressCreating headlines and subheadingsAdding images and videoAdding internal and external linksWriting meta descriptionsImproving article structureUpdating older contentAdding FAQsChecking pages for formatting errors and broken linksLearn SEO and AI Search OptimizationYou’ll gain practical experience with both traditional SEO and the emerging world of AI search / Generative Engine Optimization (GEO).You may help with:Keyword researchSearch-intent researchHeadlines and metadataInternal linkingFAQsResearch citationsImproving existing articlesStructuring content so it can be discovered through Google, ChatGPT and other AI/search platformsUsing Whitelabel SEO productsHelp Build Our Content EngineWe have a large archive of original books, articles, talks, frameworks and ideas.You’ll help us make better use of it by:Organizing contentIdentifying material worth republishing or repurposingMaintaining a content calendarTracking what has been publishedFinding opportunities to turn older content into something newDeveloping repeatable AI workflows that make content creation faster and betterWho We’re Looking ForThis role could be a particularly good fit for a student studying:MarketingCommunicationsJournalismMediaBusinessEntrepreneurshipPsychologyEnglishFilm / VideoDesignTechnology / AIBut your major matters much less than your abilities and interests.We’re looking for someone who:Writes clearly and accuratelyIs interested in generative AIHas experimented with tools such as ChatGPT and HeyGenUses social media and understands what makes people stop and pay attentionHas good visual and editorial tasteIs organized and dependableNotices detailsIs comfortable trying things they haven't done beforeCan work independently once given a clear briefIs interested in ideas, business, psychology, technology, or leadershipWants to learn and grow rapidly with support and feedbackMost importantly, we want someone who can distinguish between good AI-assisted content and generic AI-generated content.Helpful Skills — But Not RequiredExperience with any of these is useful:ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or other AI toolsCanvaCapCut or video-editing softwareWixWordPressSubstackLinkedInInstagramTikTokYouTube StudioAI image-generation toolsAI video-generation toolsGoogle AnalyticsSearch ConsoleSEO toolsYou do not need to know all of these.Part of the internship is learning new platforms, experimenting with emerging tools, and figuring out better ways of doing things.What You’ll LearnThis internship will give you hands-on experience in a rapidly emerging area of marketing: how to combine original human ideas with AI-powered content production and distribution.You’ll develop practical skills in:Generative AIPrompting and AI workflowsContent marketingSocial media marketingShort-form videoAI video productionCopywriting and editingSEOAI search / GEOWebsite publishingPersonal brandingB2B marketingContent strategyAnalytics and experimentationYou’ll also have the opportunity to create real, published work that can become part of your professional portfolio. jobs.description: Employer: BCM One Expires: 10/19/2026 BCM One is looking for Fall/Winter Interns! Come Launch Your Career With Us! Looking for more than an internship? At BCM One, you'll gain hands-on experience, work on meaningful projects, collaborate with experienced professionals, and develop skills that will prepare you for your future career. As a Marketing Intern, you'll support a variety of marketing initiatives while learning how modern marketing organizations drive awareness, engagement, and demand. You'll gain exposure to content marketing, social media, account-based marketing (ABM), AI-powered marketing tools, event planning, and campaign execution while contributing to programs that directly support BCM One's growth objectives. Work Locations: Candidates based near one of the following offices will be prioritized: Blue Bell, PA; Grand Rapids, MI; Herndon, VA; Alpharetta, GA. Candidates remote in the USA will be considered. Candidates must reside in and be authorized to work in the United States. This role is not eligible for relocation assistance or visa sponsorship. What You'll DoCreate AI-powered marketing content, including blogs, playbooks, customer-facing guides, and sales enablement materialsDevelop, schedule, and manage social media content across multiple platformsSupport Account-Based Marketing (ABM) campaigns through research, content development, and campaign executionAssist with marketing event planning, coordination, and logisticsCollaborate with marketing team members on integrated demand generation campaignsConduct market, customer, and competitive research to support campaign initiativesTrack campaign performance metrics and help identify opportunities for optimizationContribute ideas and insights to support BCM One's brand awareness and customer engagement efforts What We're Looking ForRequired QualificationsPursuing a degree in Marketing, Communications, Business, or a related fieldFamiliarity with Canva and Adobe Creative SuiteStrong teamwork skills with the ability to work independently on assigned projectsBasic understanding of marketing concepts, including campaigns, demand generation, content marketing, and social mediaStrong written and verbal communication skillsHighly organized with strong attention to detailCreative thinker with a willingness to learn and experiment with new ideasPreferred QualificationsRecent grads, graduate students or candidates in their senior yearExperience creating content for social media, blogs, websites, or school organizationsFamiliarity with marketing platforms, CRM systems, or AI tools through coursework or personal projectsInterest in B2B marketing, technology, telecommunications, or professional servicesBasic understanding of digital marketing analytics and performance measurement What You Will GainBy the end of your internship, you'll have:Hands-on experience supporting integrated marketing campaigns from concept through executionExposure to content marketing, social media management, demand generation, and account-based marketing strategiesExperience using AI-powered tools to enhance content development and marketing efficiencyInsight into how sales and marketing teams collaborate to drive business growthOpportunities to work with industry-leading marketing technologies and business platformsEnhanced project management, communication, and content creation skillsMentorship from experienced marketing professionalsA portfolio of meaningful work and real-world marketing experience you can carry into your career What Our Interns Say"I gained hands-on experience across content marketing, AI, sales enablement, and partner marketing while learning how each contributes to a larger marketing and sales strategy. One of my biggest takeaways was seeing how closely sales and marketing work together and how the strongest strategies are built when both teams align around the customer." "Throughout my internship, I had the opportunity to work on meaningful projects, collaborate with experienced professionals, and build skills that I know will benefit me throughout my career. The experience gave me confidence, practical knowledge, and a deeper understanding of how business teams operate together." Why BCM One?At BCM One, interns are trusted contributors. You'll work on real projects, collaborate with experienced professionals, and gain practical experience that extends far beyond the classroom. We believe the best learning happens when you're given meaningful work, support from great mentors, and the opportunity to make a lasting impact.Whether you're creating content, supporting campaigns, helping execute events, or learning how AI is transforming marketing, you'll leave with valuable experience and a stronger understanding of what it takes to build and grow a successful marketing organization. About BCM OneBCM One is a leading provider of NextGen Communications and Managed Services, supporting more than 18,000 business customers and 5,000 channel partners through a portfolio of cloud communications, managed services, and connectivity solutions. We are committed to delivering a world-class experience with every human interaction while creating an environment where employees can learn, grow, and make an impact. BCM One is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Strategic Marketing Intern at TADA Mobility (USA) LLC
jobs.description: Employer: TADA Mobility (USA) LLC Expires: 10/19/2026 About ThrooThroo is a Singapore-based ride-hailing platform that has disrupted the Southeast Asian market since its launch in 2018. Unlike traditional giants like Uber or Lyft, Throo operates on a zero-commission model. Instead of taking a large percentage of every fare (often 20% or more), Throo charges drivers a small, fixed platform fee. This ensures that drivers retain more of their hard-earned income and riders enjoy more competitive, transparent pricing.Powered by MVL’s blockchain, Throo creates a "fairness-first" ecosystem. By recording ride data securely and transparently, the platform incentivizes safe driving and high service quality through a token-based rewards system. Having already captured significant market share in Singapore, Cambodia, Vietnam, Thailand, and Hong Kong, Throo is now bringing its blockchain-backed, driver-centric model to the West, with New York City serving as the cornerstone of its North American expansion.About the RoleThroo is expanding, and we are looking for a Strategic Marketing Intern to join our foundational New York City Launch Team. NYC is the most competitive and regulated ride-hailing market globally. We need a high-velocity, intellectually curious individual to help build Throo’s brand from the ground up in New York City.You will work directly with the Launch Lead to create UGC content, design a localized messaging strategy, and execute the marketing playbook that will define Throo’s success in North America.Key Responsibilities1. NYC Market Entry & Messaging StrategyHyper-Local Messaging: Craft the "Why Throo" narrative specifically for the NYC market, differentiating us from incumbents (Uber/Lyft/Revel) for both driver-partners and riders.Segmented Campaigns: Develop bespoke messaging strategies for diverse NYC segments—from Manhattan commuters to outer-borough driver communities.GTM Execution: Support the end-to-end execution of the New York Go-To-Market (GTM) strategy across digital, OOH (Out-of-Home), and grassroots channels.Content Creation: Create UGC or other marketing materials to onboard New Yorkers2. Stakeholder Mapping & AdvocacyInfluence Mapping: Identify and map key NYC power players, including TLC (Taxi & Limousine Commission) influencers, driver unions/guilds, and local community leaders.Partnership Scoping: Identify and vet local NYC brand partners (lifestyle, fintech, or events) for co-marketing opportunities that provide immediate "street cred" and user trust.Public Perception: Assist in managing PR efforts to position Throo as the "fairer" alternative in the NYC transport ecosystem.What You’ll NeedNYC DNA: Deep familiarity with the New York City landscape, culture, and transit habits.Creativity Mindset: Positive, experimental approach to content creationStrategic Rigor: Ability to map complex stakeholder ecosystems and translate "fairness" into a compelling, high-conversion marketing hook.Communication: "First-class" written and verbal skills; ability to hold your own in a room with senior leadership and external partners.Why This Role?Zero-to-One Experience: You aren't maintaining a brand; you are building one in the world's most famous city.High Visibility: As part of a lean launch team, your work on messaging and stakeholder mapping will be seen and used by Throo’s global leadership.Impact: Direct involvement in one of the most significant milestones in Throo’s company history.

jobs.title: Nonprofit Accelerator Internship at University Impact
jobs.description: Employer: University Impact Expires: 10/21/2026 Nonprofit Accelerator Internship – UI Charitable Outcomes Lab(Priority Applications Due 9.25.2026) BackgroundUI Charitable helps financial advisors and their clients give more impactfully. We work with ~1,300 families and ~400 financial advisors, and we manage $500+ million in charitable assets. More importantly, we have moved over $350 million out the door to nonprofits and impact investments working to improve the world's most pressing social and environmental issues. Why We Think This Work Matters NowTwo forces are about to reshape philanthropy. The AI boom is creating a new generation of wealth, and the founders and employees holding that ownership are deciding how to structure their giving. Most of them will want to move money out faster than the sector can absorb it. Over the same period, as much as $124 trillion will change hands through 2048, with an anticipated $18 trillion of it going to charity. We are building the infrastructure to turn that money into real improvements in people's lives. The Problem You Will Work on For This InternshipA lot of charitable dollars do not produce the lasting change donors expect. Plenty of funded organizations will never solve the problem they exist to solve, and money alone will not fix that. Most attempts to address this try to change donor behavior, including several of our own. So we are working on the organizations instead. What We Are BuildingEight years of building the infrastructure gives us a direct relationship with thousands of nonprofits our donors already fund. We want to help them become more effective. The closest analogy is a business accelerator for nonprofits, or a private equity operating team. We assess an organization across the core functions of a well-run business, run it through a cohort based program, and reassess later to see what moved. So far we have a literature review, a survey of 150 nonprofits, an analysis of our own data, and some first drafts of our curriculum and a way we will measure the success of the program. We will judge the program by whether those organizations actually improve, not by how many attend. The Eight Functions We want all organizations our donors give to, to have a sound understanding of their outcomes and impact. But in order to do that, you have to be running an effective/efficient organization. We are organizing the program around the functions that separate organizations that grow from organizations that stall. Each intern will own work across multiple of these functions.Fundraising and the growth engine. Treating donor development as a sales pipeline with stages, conversion rates, and follow-up. (Sales, Marketing, and Branding)AI adoption and operations. Where AI can take real work off a five-person staff. Marketing and branding. Making the case for support to people who have never heard of the organization.Board development and governance. What effective boards do, and how to get a board to do it.Program measurement and evaluation. Outputs, outcomes, and impact, and how small organizations can measure honestly without a research budget. (Public Health, Statistics, etc.)Finance, accounting, and internal controls. Who approves spending, who reconciles accounts, and what gets outsourced.Technology and data systems. CRM, donor records, and reporting that does not live in the executive director’s head.Talent and leadership capacity. Hiring, retention, and how a small team allocates the hours it has. Position OverviewWe are hiring two interns to help run a year-long pilot. You will work directly with Gary McHardy (a Rhodes Scholar based in South Africa) and Tanner Mills (Sr. Associate at UI Charitable). The team is small and the program is new, which means you will own real pieces of the work rather than support someone else’s. You will interview nonprofit CEOs, build the assessment instruments, write and deliver curriculum, and sit in on calls with the senior advisors guiding the program. Duties and Responsibilities:Design the curriculum. Build the workshop content, templates, and tools for your assigned functions, covering what the best organizations do and how a five-person staff can actually do it.Deliver it. Run webinars, cohort sessions, and office hours. You will be the one teaching, not just organizing.Drive results at the organizations. Work directly with participating nonprofits to implement what the curriculum covers. The goal is a CRM that exists, a pipeline that gets worked, a board that shows up.Interview nonprofit leaders. Run discovery calls, take structured notes, and turn what you hear into changes to the program.Analyze the data. Segment organizations by size, growth trend, and reported need using assessment results and public financials.Measure our own results and make adjustments. Track baseline and follow-up scores and report the delta honestly, including where we did not move the needle.The above list is not exhaustive; additional tasks will for sure be assigned as necessary. Required Skills/Abilities:Communication Skills: Strong written and verbal communication. You will be talking with nonprofit executives and delivering material they will read.Analytical Skills: Able to work with survey and financial data, draw conclusions, and present findings clearly and concisely.Project Management Skills: Able to handle several workstreams at once, prioritize, and hit deadlines without being chased.Comfort with Ambiguity: This program does not exist yet. You should be comfortable proposing an approach, testing it, and changing it when it fails.Team Coordination: Work very well with other people as a high output team. Deliver on what you’re responsible for AI Fluency: Regular use of AI tools for research, drafting, and analysis, with the judgment to check the output.Problem-Solving Skills: The ability to break a large, vague problem into pieces someone can actually work on.Humility and a Desire to Learn: A strong interest in understanding UI Charitable’s tools and programs and their role in achieving social impact.Integrity: Keep commitments, admit mistakes, maintain confidentiality where appropriate, and act in the organization’s best interests at all times. Education and Experience:Currently pursuing or recently completed a bachelor’s degree. Business, economics, statistics, public health, public policy, marketing, computer science and communications backgrounds all fit.Coursework, work experience, or genuine interest in at least one of the eight functions listed above. Tell us which one or two in your application.Proficiency with spreadsheets, survey tools, and standard office applications.Prior nonprofit experience is welcome but not required. Physical Requirements:Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer. The expectation is that candidates would be able to commit 20 hours per week, in person. How to ApplyEmail Tanner at tanner@uicharitable.org with your resume and a short note, under 250 words. Tell us which of the eight functions you would most want to own, why you want to work on this, and about anything you have produced, built, sold, raised, or automated. EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITYUI Charitable offers fair and equal employment opportunity to all qualified job candidates regardless of age, race, religion, color, sex, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, arrest record, conviction record, physical disability, developmental disability, national origin, membership in the National Guard, state defense force or any other reserve component of the military forces of the United States or Utah, genetic information, marital status, or any legally protected status.

About BNP Paribas:BNP Paribas is a leading bank in Europe with an international reach across the US, EMEA and APAC. It has a presence in 65 countries, with nearly 190,000 employees. The bank employs over 3,500 people in offices in the US across 10 states including New York, Jersey City, Chesterbrook, PA, San Francisco, Boston, Chicago, Denver, Miami, and Washington, DC. BNP Paribas has built a strong and diversified presence to support its client base. We continue to grow and strengthen our commitment to the US market through our Corporate & Institutional Banking activities. We are one of a few non-US banks to offer a full value chain for our clients, from trading to financing, and clearing and custody in the US with the international footprint and capacity to deliver both globally and locally. Leveraging the strength of our European roots, our network can support clients in virtually every region of the world, enabling more connectivity and efficiency wherever our clients conduct business. We take pride in our expertise and our ability to adapt while constantly looking ahead to create a more sustainable world. As an international company with a global footprint, the unique cultures and viewpoints of our team members are an integral part of the fabric of BNP Paribas. We are a company with a purpose - to be a responsible and sustainable global leader. We aim to create an environment where our employees feel empowered to drive change, make an impact and be true to themselves. We employ talented individuals from a wide variety of backgrounds, locally and globally, and are inspired by our employees who help us in cultivating a diverse, equitable and inclusive workplace through initiatives such as our Diversity, Equity & Inclusion (DEI) Leadership Forum and Employee Resource Group (ERG) communities. We strive to be a workplace where all team members can grow and thrive and offer robust training, development, and mentoring opportunities to make that vision a reality. Our leaders are deeply committed to DEI and highly accessible to our employees, consistently soliciting feedback on how we can continue to support our employees to reach their highest potential. jobs.title: Marketing & Growth Lead at Forbidden Well
jobs.description: Employer: Forbidden Well Expires: 10/22/2026 Marketing & Growth Lead (Paid Internship → Full-Time)Forbidden Well · New York, NY · Hybrid, 2 days a week on site$1,500/month · 90-day paid internship, designed to convert to full-time This is a six-figure job on the other side of 90 days.The internship pays $1,500/month. The full-time role it converts into starts at $75,000 and can exceed $150,000 based on performance and the revenue you generate. We built the path that way on purpose — we'd rather pay it out than not. You will own marketing. All of it.This is not an internship where you're handed a task list and asked to schedule someone else's posts. You will own the strategy, the calendar, the campaigns and the creative. The concepts are yours. The pitch ideas are yours. The call on what we run next is yours.We'll work alongside you to stay aligned on direction and make sure you have what you need, but you are not waiting on us to tell you what to do. If you need someone to hand you assignments, this is the wrong job. If you've been waiting for someone to hand you the keys instead, read on. You are the keeper of the brandForbidden Well should look and sound like one thing everywhere we show up: email campaigns, social posts, stories, the grid, and every other form of communication we put out. Someone should be able to see any piece of our content and know instantly that it's us.That means more than staying consistent. You'll continuously fine-tune that identity, stay organized in how we market, and be deliberate about what goes out and why. No random posting. Every piece has a purpose you can explain.You own every external relationshipThis role owns all points of contact with other spas, vendors, modeling agencies and brands — curating them, organizing them, and keeping them alive over time.A real example: a friend recently connected us to the owner of a very successful spa in Miami. We make the introduction, and from there it's yours to develop into something lucrative — a referral partnership where their clients coming to New York come to us, and ours heading to Miami go to them. First introduction to signed, working partnership, end to end. That's the job. What you'll runBrand, content and social across Instagram and TikTok: your concepts, your voice, your calendarBrand consistency across every channel we touch, and the standards that keep it that wayEmail marketing, including weekly campaigns and automated flowsPaid social and lead generation campaigns with our agency partnerPartnerships and outreach: spas, vendors, modeling agencies and like-minded brands, plus the co-marketing campaigns that come out of themPhoto and video shoots: concept, casting, scheduling and running the dayOur podcast, using our full in-house studio: booking guests, recording, editing and publishingLocal search, our Google Business Profile and our Google reviews programDaily and weekly reporting on what's working Who this is forYou generate ideas without being asked and can defend themYou write well and have taste. You can tell the difference between good and almost goodYou have an eye for consistency and it bothers you when something is off-brandYou're comfortable talking to people and turning an introduction into a relationship that lastsYou're comfortable with AI tools, especially Claude, and use them to move fasterYou're organized enough to run a shoot, a podcast taping and three campaigns in the same weekYou want to build something, not pad a resume Where it goesThis 90-day period is a prerequisite for a full-time, long-term role, and it's how we both find out if this is the right fit. We're hiring for the person who runs marketing at Forbidden Well for years — someone who grows as the company does and takes on more as we open more. If you hit the benchmarks, which we'll set with you and review together, the full-time role starts at $75,000 and can exceed $150,000 based on performance and revenue generated. About usForbidden Well is a luxury wellness house in New York built around IV therapy, advanced treatments and a client experience that feels like nothing else in the city.Apply with your resume and anything you've made that you're proud of: content, campaigns, a brand you built, a project that worked. Tell us about one brand whose identity you think is airtight and why, and one relationship or partnership you started and kept going. We care more about what you've shipped than where you've interned.

Expires: 10/22/2026 Job SummarySpend Your Summer Making an Impact Are you the person who always asks "Why do we do it that way?" and then starts thinking of a better way? Clark National Accounts, a division of Clark Associates, is looking for a Project Management Intern to join our Project Services team for the summer. This isn't a coffee-running internship. You'll get hands-on exposure to how large-scale restaurant and retail projects come to life while owning real process improvement initiatives that help our team work smarter as we continue to grow. If you're curious, driven, love solving problems, and want to see how a fast-paced business operates behind the scenes, we'd love to meet you. Who Are We? Clark National Accounts partners with some of the largest restaurant, retail, entertainment, healthcare, hospitality, and senior living brands in the country. We help our customers successfully open new locations by providing equipment, supplies, project management, logistics coordination, and operational expertise. jobs.description: Employer: Graco Inc. Expires: 10/22/2026 The purpose of this position is to provide immersive, strategic-level experience within Graco’s Category Marketing team. At Graco, Category Marketing focuses on understanding and growing specific customer segments and industries (often referred to as market verticals), helping the business identify opportunities, understand customer needs, and shape strategies that drive growth. In this role, the intern will lead a defined strategic project for an assigned customer segment under the mentorship of the Director of Category Marketing. The intern will leverage market research, Voice of Customer (VOC) insights, competitive analysis, and go-to-market strategy to address a real business challenge. The experience culminates in the development and presentation of a strategic recommendation to Graco’s Executive Leadership Team. This internship is designed for MBA candidates seeking a long-term career in category marketing, product marketing, strategic marketing, or general management. Program Structure: This summer internship is centered on a high-value strategic project that addresses a real business opportunity or challenge within an assigned category and which has the potential to shape future growth initiatives. The project is supplemented by exposure to the broader category marketing function and close collaboration with cross-functional partners, including product management, channel marketing, corporate marketing, and sales. The internship culminates in a strategic recommendation presented to senior internship. What You Will Do at Graco Strategic Project Experience Lead a high-impact strategic project focused on a real business opportunity or challenge within an assigned customer segment or industry. Work closely with a Category Marketing leader to define the project scope, conduct analysis, and develop recommendations. Apply market research, customer insights, and business strategy concepts to address a meaningful business question. Develop and present a final recommendation to senior leaders at the conclusion of the internship. Market and Customer Insights Conduct market, customer, and competitive research to better understand industry trends and customer needs. Analyze Voice of Customer (VOC) feedback and other data sources to identify key insights and opportunities. Learn how customer and market insights are used to shape busness and marketing strategies. Cross-Functional Collaboration Collaborate with teams across product management, sales, channel marketing, and corporate marketing Gain exposure to how strategy is developed and translated into product launches, marketing campaigns, and commercial execution. Coordinate with internal subject matter experts to validate research findings and assumptions. Participate in team meetings, project reviews, and business discussions to better understand Graco's growth strategy. Professional Development Build skills in strategic thinking, business analysis, executive communication, and problem solving. Receive coaching and mentorship from experienced marketing leaders throughout the internship. Develop and deliver a professional executive-level presentation summarizing project findings and recommendations. Other duties and learning opportunities as assigned.
